title: UNIT FIVE: POLITICS, ECONOMY, AND SOCIAL PROCESSES FROM THE EARLY SIXTEENTH TO THE END OF THE EIGHTEENTH CENTURIES
content:
ከሰላምታ በላይ በሆነ ጥልቅ ፍቅር እና ቁርኝት! እጅግ የምንወዳችሁና የምንኮራባችሁ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦቻችን! 💖✨👋 እንደምን ሰነበታችሁልን? ዛሬ ደግሞ የHistory of Ethiopia and the Horn (Hist. 1012) የምዕራፍ አምስት ማጠቃለያ የሆነውን Part 4 Tutorial ይዘንላችሁ ቀርበናል! በዚህ ክፍል በምዕራፍ 5 ክፍል 5.6 እና 5.6.1-5.6.2 ስር የሚገኙትን የጎንደር ዘመን (Gondarine Period)፣ የስነ-ሕንፃና የባህል እድገቶች እንዲሁም የዘመነ መሳፍንት (Zemene-Mesafint) ታሪክ በዝርዝር እንመለከታለን። በፈተና ላይ 100% ውጤት እንደምታመጡ በሚያረጋግጥ መልኩ በጥቅል እንግሊዝኛ ማብራሪያ፣ በቴክኒካዊ አማርኛ ትርጉም፣ በExam Hints እና አዝናኝ ቀልዶች አዘጋጅተንላችኋል። እስከ መጨረሻው በትኩረት አብራችሁን ቆዩ👇👇👇! ☕📚🔥

5.6. The Gondarine Period and Zemene-Mesafint

5.6.1. The Gondarine Period (1630-1780s)

• Political Developments:
- The Gondarine period, which lasted for about 130 years, can be sub-divided into three distinct phases based on political and cultural criteria: foundation and glory (1630–1706), insecurity (1706–1720), and revival and steady decline (1720–1780s).
- The establishment of a permanent royal capital at Gondar in 1636 by Emperor Fasilede followed earlier mobile and semi-permanent capitals around Lake Tana, such as Enfraaz (Emperor Sartsa-Dengel in 1571) and sites like Qoga, Gorgora, Danqaz, and Azazo under Emperor Susenyos.
- Strategic reasons for choosing Gondar as the capital included: directly supervising customs on the Red Sea–Lake Tana–Enarya trade route, proximity to the main caravan route from Mettema to Lake Tana, protective semi-circular mountain ranges surrounding the town, and safe distance from malaria-infested lower regions of Lake Tana.
- Gondar reached its height of political power during the reigns of Fasilede (r. 1632–67) and Iyasu I (r. 1682–1706; Adyam Saggad). Fasilede re-established the Orthodox Alexandrian faith and expelled the Jesuits. Iyasu I restored state control over vast territories, obtained vassalage from Musa (Na'ib of Massawa), reached Enarya in 1704, extended symbolic presence in Tigray and Shewa, and introduced tax, land, and customs reforms. He is regarded as the last powerful emperor before Tewodros II.
- Political instability began in 1706 following the assassination of Iyasu I by a faction led by his son, Tekle-Haymanot. This ushered in a period of court intrigues and monarchical poisonings: Tekle-Haymanot was assassinated in 1708, Tewoflos was killed in 1711, Yostos was poisoned in 1717, and Dawit III was poisoned in 1721.
- A temporary revival occurred with Emperor Bakkafa (r. 1721–1730), who strengthened the army using Oromo units and benefited from his consort, Etege Mentewab (Berhan Mogasa). After Bakkafa's death in 1730, decline set in as three regional factions competed to control the power of the *ras bitwedded* (king-maker):
1. The *qwaregnoch* faction led by Etege Mentewab and her kinsmen from Qwara.
2. The Oromo faction from Wollo led by maternal uncles of Iyasu II (following Mentewab's arrangement of a marriage between her son Iyasu II and Wubit of Wollo).
3. The Tigray faction led by Ras Mikael Sehul, invited by Mentewab to counterbalance Oromo influence. Ras Mikael killed Emperor Iyoas in 1769 and enthroned Yohannes II, establishing regional warlord supremacy over the monarchy.

• Cultural Achievements of the Gondarine Period:
- Often termed the

Gondar served as a hub for administration, commerce, education, literature, fine arts, and crafts for over two centuries.
- Architecture: Famous for stone castles, bridges, libraries, baths, towers, and fortifications within the *Fasil Gebbi* compound built by Fasilede, Yohannes I, Iyasu I, Dawit III, Bakkafa, and Queen Mentewab. Architectural foundations predated Gondar itself, starting with Emperor Sartsa-Dengel's castle at Guzara (c. 1586) and bridges over the Garno River, as well as Emperor Susenyos's bridge over the Blue Nile at Alata.
- Painting: Rich tradition of religious illuminations on manuscripts, wood, cross designs, and church walls (especially churches sponsored by Queen Mentewab).
- Literature: Active production of royal chronicles, hagiographies (Lives of Saints), Miracles of Mary, litanies, and liturgical poetry/music.
- Trade and Urbanization: Established Ethiopia's first daily market. Foreign communities included Iberians, Indians, Greeks, and Armenians, with a population reaching 60,000–70,000. Served as a religious center for Christians, Muslims, and Bete Israel, housing elite Orthodox education centers across four levels: *Nebab Bet* (reading), *Qedasse Bet* (liturgy), *Zema Bet* (music), *Qene Bet* (poetry), and *Metsehaf Bet* (interpretation of holy books) along with *aqwaqwam* instruction.

👉
1. የጎንደር ዘመን ሦስት ክፍሎች (Gondarine Period): የእድገትና የክብር (1630-1706)፣ ያለመረጋጋት (1706-1720)፣ እና የመንሰራራትና ውድቀት (1720-1780s) በመባል ይከፈላል።
2. ጎንደር መዲና የሆነችበት ምክንያት: አጼ ፋሲለደስ በ1636 ጎንደርን ቋሚ መዲና አደረገ። ምክንያቱም የንግድ መስመሮችን ለመቆጣጠር፣ ከተራሮች ጥቃትን ለመከላከል እና ከወባ በሽታ ለመራቅ ነው።
3. የፖለቲካ ውዥንብር: አጼ ኢያሱ 1ኛ በ1706 ከተገደለ በኋላ የንጉሦች መመረዝ እና መገደል ተስፋፋ። በኋለኞች ጊዜያት ሦስት ቡድኖች (የቋራው *ቋረኞች*፣ የወሎው ኦሮሞ እና የትግራዩ ራስ ሚካኤል ስሑል) ሥልጣን ለመያዝ ተፋለሙ። በ1769 ራስ ሚካኤል እዮአስን በመግደል የክልል መሳፍንትን የበላይነት አረጋገጠ።
4. ባህላዊና ስነ-ሕንፃዊ ስኬቶች: የፋሲል ግቢ ግንቦች፣ የጉዛራ ቤተ-መንግሥትና የዓላጣ ድልድይ፣ የመጀመሪያው የዕለት ገበያ፣ እና አራቱ የአብነት ትምህርት ቤቶች (*ንባብ፣ ቅዳሴ፣ ዜማ/አቋቋም፣ ቅኔ፣ መጽሐፍ ቤት*) የጎንደር ወርቃማ ስኬቶች ናቸው።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Founder of Gondar Capital (1636): Emperor Fasilede.
• Last Powerful Gondarine Monarch: Iyasu I (Iyasu the Great).
• Architectural Antecedents to Gondar: Guzara Castle (Sartsa-Dengel) & Alata Bridge (Susenyos).
• King Maker of 1769: Ras Mikael Sehul of Tigray.
• Four Levels of Church Education: Nebab Bet, Qedasse Bet, Zema/Qene Bet, Metsehaf Bet.

😂 የታሪክ ቀልድ: በጎንደር ዘመን እኮ ዘውድ መጫንና መመረዝ እኩል ነበሩ፤ ዙፋን ላይ የተቀመጠ ንጉሥ ቀጣዩ የሻይ ሰዓት ከመድረሱ በፊት መመረዙን ወይም አለመመረዙን ያረጋግጥ ነበር! ☕🐍🏰


5.6.2. The Zemene-Mesafint (Era of Princes, 1786-1853)

• Origin and Chronology:
- The *Zemene-Mesafint* refers to a period of political decentralization characterized by the decay of supreme imperial authority and the rise of autonomous regional lords.
- Chronologically dated from 1786 (ascent to power of Ras Ali I, founder of the Yejju/Warraseh Dynasty) to 1853 (defeat of the last Yejju prince, Ras Ali II, by Dajjach Kasa Haylu/Emperor Tewodros II at the Battle of Ayshal).
- The structural breakdown began when Ras Mikael Sehul deposed King Iyoas in 1769. Severe measures against nobility made Ras Mikael unpopular, leading to his defeat by a coalition of lords from Gojjam, Amhara, Lasta, and Wollo at the Battle of Sarbakussa in 1771.
- Major political regions dominated by regional warlords included Tigray, Semen, Dembiya, Begemedir, Lasta, Yejju, Wollo, Damot, Mecha, and Gojjam.

• The Yejju Dynasty Dominance:
- The Yejju (Warraseh) dynasty from Debre Tabor served as the central king-makers for over seven decades.
- Peak Yejju power was achieved under Gugsa Marso (r. 1803–1825), who fought continuous struggles against Ras Walde-Silassie of Enderta and Dejjazmatch Sabagadis Woldu of Agame.
- Yimam (r. 1825–1828; son of Gugsa) defeated Hayle-Mariam Gebre of Simen in 1826. Marye (r. 1828–1831; brother of Yimam) fought Sabagadis at the Battle of May Aslamay (Dabra Abay) in 1831, where both leaders died, though Yejju secured victory.

• Major Features of Zemene-Mesafint:
- Shift from strong central imperial power to a multi-centered decentralized political system.
- Reduction of the Gondarine emperor to a puppet ruler who

.
- Continuous internal warfare among regional lords competing to control the emperor in Gondar.
- Christological doctrinal controversies dividing the Orthodox Church into regional factions.
- Decline in classical Gondarine literature, architecture, and visual arts.
- Breakdown of the military regimental system, forcing emperors to depend completely on regional lords.
- Peaceful consolidation and independence of outlying principalities such as the Kingdom of Shewa.
- Autonomous foreign contacts and alliances established directly between regional lords and foreign powers.

• Other Developments and Historical Significance of Zemene-Mesafint:
- The Emperor remained a vital symbol of national political unity and source of dynastic legitimacy.
- Yejju elites strove to maintain the territorial integrity and structural unity of the realm.
- Regional lords only fought to be

(*ras bitwedded*) rather than taking the imperial throne directly, preserving the Solomonic myth.
- Decentralization expanded courtly culture, music, and traditions beyond Gondar into regional seats.
- Fusion of regional and ethnic cultural elements enriched national diversity.
- Internal conflicts forged experienced independent regional kingdoms that later spearheaded 19th-century Ethiopian reunification.

👉
1. የዘመነ መሳፍንት መጀመሪያና መጨረሻ: ከ1786 (የየጁው ራስ አሊ 1ኛ ወደ ሥልጣን መምጣት) እስከ 1853 (የራስ አሊ 2ኛ በካሳ ሃይሉ/አጼ ቴዎድሮስ በአይሻል ውጊያ መሸነፍ) የነበረ ጊዜ ነው።
2. የየጁ ሥረወ-መንግሥት (Yejju Dynasty): ዋና መዲናቸውን ደብረ ታቦር በማድረግ ከ70 ዓመታት በላይ ንጉሥ ሰሪ (*King-maker*) ሆነው ቆይተዋል። ራስ ጉግሳ ማርሶ፣ ይማም፣ እና ማርየ ዋና ዋና መሪዎቻቸው ነበሩ።
3. ዋና ዋና መግለጫዎች: ንጉሡ ሥልጣን የሌለው

መሆኑ፣ የቤተ-ክርስቲያን በሃይማኖታዊ ክርክሮች መከፋፈል፣ የጎንደር ጥበባትና ስነ-ጽሑፍ መንሸራተት፣ እና እንደ ሸዋ ያሉ መንግሥታት በተረጋጋ ሁኔታ መጠናከራቸው ናቸው።
4. በጎ ጎኖችና አወንታዊ ገጽታዎች: ንጉሡ የብሔራዊ አንድነት ምልክት ሆኖ መቀጠሉ፣ መሳፍንቱ ንጉሥ ሰሪ እንጂ ራሳቸው ንጉሥ ለመሆን አለመሞከራቸው፣ የቤተ-መንግሥት ባህል ወደ ክልሎች መስፋፋቱ እና ለ19ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን የኢትዮጵያ አንድነት መፈጠር መንገድ መክፈቱ ነው።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Start and End Battles/Events of Zemene-Mesafint: 1786 (Ras Ali I) to 1853 (Battle of Ayshal - Kasa Haylu defeats Ras Ali II).
• Battle where Ras Mikael Sehul was Defeated (1771): Battle of Sarbakussa.
• Battle of May Aslamay/Dabra Abay (1831): Death of both Marye of Yejju & Sabagadis of Agame.
• Capital of Yejju Dynasty: Debre Tabor.
• Status of the Emperor during Zemene-Mesafint: Reigned but did not rule (Puppet King).

😂 የታሪክ ቀልድ: በዘመነ መሳፍንት ጊዜ የጎንደር ንጉሥ መሆን ማለት የካርቶን አሻንጉሊት ከመሆን አይለይም፤ ስምህ ይጠራል፣ ዘውድ ትደፋለህ... ግን ውሳኔውን በሙሉ የሚያሳልፈው ደብረ ታቦር የተቀመጠው የየጁ ራስ ነው! 👑👑⚔️
